title: Boundary normal coordinates and quadratic window transfer
reviewed_arguments: All 33 original obligations, all 31 unchanged displays, three unchanged complete solutions and the original exact diagram remain.

NC1 retains the full smooth single-face scalar wave form, time-variable coefficients, spatial positivity, only boundary vanishing of the cross block, arbitrary complex lower matrices and both weak domains.

The enlarged autonomous smooth flow supplies all parameter derivatives and a backward inverse. The inverse matrix ODE establishes determinant nonvanishing throughout the common interval without assuming it.
Boundary vanishing gives exact quadratic identity jets in every parameter. The cotangent map includes the Y_t time shift and proves the full symplectic identity.
The Schur complement, transformed quadratic normal symbol, all boundary jets, negative scalar multiplier, Hamilton covariance and geometric entry conditions are proved.
The full compressed bundle map and its inverse preserve the embedded boundary tangential bundle. They are defined on all covectors.
The H1 and H1_0 maps use actual approximation, compact substitution, weak derivative limits and inverse maps. Natural-dual transport acts on the full form domain and retains the Jacobian.
The complete b-operator class and actual formal adjoints imply finite and one-neighborhood smooth-wavefront covariance.
Every weak coefficient transforms with its correct indices, density and original matrix order. The scalar multiplier contributes its full derivative term and preserves boundary-nonzero tests.
Every ordinary characteristic lift has both-sign time ellipticity. The normalized coordinate errors are uniformly quadratic in the boundary defining function.
The gliding field reverses the analytic clock by a positive anchor-dependent factor. The two center flows agree to second order with an explicit uniform constant.
The full U064 criterion supplies witnesses for every small signed step. Their transfer has the exact fourth-order coordinate error and uniform quadratic window.
The lifted front is relatively closed off forcing; all normalized characteristic lifts remain in the fixed compact patch.
The normalized RW4 criterion and GF32 secant condition hold for the full NC1 coefficient class, removing the earlier b-identically-zero collar restriction.
The exact time-dependent example and all three solutions retain the time shift, boundary functional and explicit 269 window constant.
Five finite groups with 97 cases supplement the proofs. All sixteen final lesson captures were inspected; all mobile formula extents were measured.
